data.title: Accenture agrees to pay $25M DOJ settlement over DEI policies
data.description:
Accenture (ACN) has reportedly agreed to pay $25 million to resolve allegations by the U.S. Justice Department that it took race and sex into consideration when making hiring and promotion decisions.

According to a Bloomberg report, the Justice Department said that Accenture engaged in discriminatory employment practices when it falsely certified compliance with regulations on government contracts prohibiting such practices.

The management and technology consulting company did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The government alleged Accenture was working toward what one employee described as “stealth goals” to achieve race and sex-based targets for the makeup of the workforce in its various units, the report said, adding that the government said in the settlement agreement the workforce demographic goals were documented internally in monthly reports.

The allegations stemmed from 2017 to the present, according to the Bloomberg report, which cited the Justice Department. Accenture’s practices also affected training and educational opportunities, the report added.

data.title: SA Asks: How can the U.S. government realistically regulate AI safety?
data.description:
How can the U.S. government realistically regulate AI development and safety to help ensure that the technology doesn't harm humans?

Seeking Alpha analysts Luca Socci, Julia Ostian, and Jonathan Weber weigh in.

Luca Socci: Regulating AI safety is a matter of balancing the necessary speed to be on top of the AI race and a framework that protects human users from potential harm and threats. I see four main aspects that will have to be considered. 

First, human accountability should not be delegable. Here legislation could develop a multi-tier framework where high-risk decisions can't be legally executed without being able to clearly identify the human being behind the choice who bears legal liability for it. 

Second, a lot of power is concentrated in a handful of AI labs, which could create new oligarchies. I think it would be interesting to promote labor-level participation boards so that workers could have a seat and be part of the governance. I also think that mandating interoperability so that data access requirements are equal for everyone could be part of this. 

A third aspect would be a requirement to show that AI implementation doesn't negatively impact workers' lives and their mental health or increase unemployment. There could be a framework that incentivizes and favors companies that, because of AI implementation, hire more and invest more in human capital. 

The final aspect of a regulatory framework could be to develop clear standards for what is now the largest infrastructure buildout of the century. Here, algorithmic distribution could be regulated so that we can better track or watermark how these models work, where they come from, and how they are commercialized.

Julia Ostian: This is a great question, and I believe a complete answer will take years, if not a decade, to get. AI is changing and evolving faster than anything we've seen in the tech industry before, which is an innovative world by itself. Law and regulation take much longer to decide and implement. 

This is why, I believe, the first step in the regulatory process should be recognizing automated AI agents and their actions as the full responsibility and liability of the companies that create them or the frontier labs. Of course, the extent of the responsibility should be discussed further. 

The next important thing would be recognizing agents with taken-down guardrails as cyberweapons, which also should be regulated by the Department of Defense. 

The situation with OpenAI (OPENAI) and Hugging Face, which Nvidia (NVDA) decided to acquire, is a perfect example of that. An agent was given hacking tools and freed from its guardrails, which resulted in it breaking into the Hugging Face database. In this case, OpenAI (OPENAI) made a mistake; it was not a case of an AI agent "gone rogue," and it could serve as a great precedent for regulation.

Anthropic (ANTHRO), with recent claims from its workers about the safety of AI, also has to be held accountable for its agents, as any other frontier lab. That way, there will be nothing to be concerned about regarding AI.

Jonathan Weber: Effectively regulating AI safety seems like a tough task to me. Companies aren't keen to be regulated, and if regulations are too strict, the U.S. risks falling behind China and possibly other countries in the AI race. 

I think the government should encourage companies to deploy industry best practices and to cooperate with each other when it comes to identifying risks, etc. Having new models tested by trusted players before they are rolled out to everyone is sensible as well. 

Still, with the speed OpenAI (OPENAI), Anthropic (ANTHRO), and so on come up with new models, some risk prevails and likely cannot be regulated away entirely, I believe.

data.title: Energy Recovery cut at Seaport, reflecting significant exposure to Middle East turmoil
data.description:
Energy Recovery (ERII) fell 5.4% in Monday's trading as Seaport Global downgraded the energy efficiency technology firm to Neutral from Buy after the company withdrew guidance for its desalination business, reflecting significant exposure to a Middle East market in turmoil, while the wastewater business continues to post weak results.

Seaport analyst Jeff Campbell said he likes Energy Recovery (ERII) as an ongoing monopoly in pressure exchange within large-scale desalination, the company has no debt, and it consistently generates free cash—although in varying amounts—because whatever the revenue levels in a given period, the gross margins are consistently very high for a manufactured product.

However, Energy Recovery's (ERII) desalination business is very lumpy and beyond its control, which Campbell said makes the amounts of the company's revenue and free cash flow unpredictable, with volatility verified by seemingly constant guidance revisions, and the company has not found another business where its pressure exchange technology provides the outsized benefits that it provides to desalination.

The analyst also warned that Energy Recovery's (ERII) business is highly concentrated in what has emerged as an unstable part of the world, where not only has the development of large-scale desalination slowed, but the facilities may emerge as targets of warfare.

data.title: Apple releases long-awaited new version of Siri with greater cross-app functionality
data.description:
Apple (AAPL) has launched Siri AI, an entirely new version of its digital assistant, which features more natural conversation and greater cross-app functionality.

The beta version rolls out today in English, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish users expected to arrive in October. The new version was revealed during Apple's annual fall product event last week.

"Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding, broad world knowledge, onscreen awareness, and even more systemwide app actions," Apple said in a release. "Siri AI can help users find what they need in the moment, from answering questions on virtually any topic to surfacing relevant information from a user's messages, emails, photos, and more." 

The new version of Siri, built on Apple Intelligence, pulls from personal context to better relate and respond to a particular user. It can also utilize onscreen awareness, taking actions or answering questions based on what's on the screen.

Siri AI uses iCloud to privately sync conversational history across Apple products. Siri AI has been integrated into the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and the Vision Pro. 

The new Siri arrives in the iOS 27 update. The new Apple Intelligence features work on the iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, and all iPhone 16, 17 and 18 models. For the iPad, Apple Intelligence works on M-series devices.

The new Siri was originally intended for release in 2025. However, technical difficulties pushed its release date out until now.

data.title: Resilient corporate earnings keep U.S. equity outlook up - Wells Fargo
data.description:
Wells Fargo Investment Institute remains constructive on U.S. large-cap equities (SPY) (VOO), maintaining that rapid corporate earnings growth—rather than valuation expansion—will continue to drive stock market returns. 

Global Equity Analyst Alex Sagal highlighted a notable dynamic in 2026: the S&P 500 has gained roughly 13% year-to-date even as its 12-month forward price-to-earnings ratio compressed from roughly 22x to around 19x. This decoupling underscores the firm's thesis that earnings momentum, not multiple expansion, is now the primary engine of equity gains, Sagal wrote in a note to clients.

Second-quarter results demonstrated remarkable resilience. With nearly all S&P 500 companies having reported, revenue increased about 15%, while headline earnings jumped some 50%. Even excluding unusually large nonoperating gains, earnings advanced ~32%—the strongest pace since the post-pandemic rebound in 2021.

The index has now delivered seven consecutive quarters of double-digit earnings growth, Sagal noted, overcoming significant headwinds including Fed rate-hike prospects, long-dated yields (TLT) (ZROZ) hitting multidecade highs, a prolonged conflict with Iran, and oil prices (USO) (BNO) bouncing above $100 per barrel.

Sagal argued that lower multiples reflect a healthier dynamic: EPS growth has simply outpaced stock price appreciation. Several structural factors support continued valuation compression—higher interest rates increasing discount rates, decelerating earnings growth nearing cyclical peaks, elevated geopolitical risk, rising leverage in AI (AIQ) (AIEQ)-related financing, capital-intensive growth cycles, and greater index exposure to cyclical semiconductors (SMH) (SOXX), which now represent 15.5% of the S&P 500 compared with just 2.8% a decade ago.

Despite these pressures, Wells Fargo's outlook remains positive. Resilient earnings growth should more than offset valuation compression and continue pushing stock prices higher.

data.title: Antofagasta raised to Buy at Berneberg following copper selloff
data.description:
Copper miner Antofagasta (ANFGF) was upgraded Monday to Buy from Hold with a 4,400 pence price target at Berenberg, saying the shares are now attractively priced after copper's recent dip that followed reports that the Trump administration still has not made a decision on refined copper tariffs, which removed some of the premium in copper prices.

Berenberg does not expect the tariffs to materialize, believing the inflationary effects on the U.S. economy would prove too damaging.

Antofagasta (ANFGF) maintains quality assets in a low-risk jurisdiction, and forecasts volume growth in 2027-28 that will help drive a re-rating of the shares, the analysts said.

The bank pointed to Antofagasta's (ANFGF) strong growth pipeline as the core of its investment case and forecast the miner to lift copper production by 27% to 818K metric tons by 2028, up from 646K tons in 2026, resting on higher ore grades at the Los Pelambres mine and rising volumes from the new second concentrator at Centinela, both in Chile.

The analyst also expects free cash flow to jump as spending on new projects rolls off, rising from $700M in 2026 to $3.1B in 2027, with a 6.2% free cash flow yield.

data.title: OpenAI buys startup working on smartphone camera: report
data.description:
• OpenAI (OPENAI) has acquired Glass Imaging, a startup working on creating a smartphone camera, The Wall Street Journal reported.
  • The acquisition valued Glass Imaging at more than $300M, the news outlet added, citing people familiar with the matter. The startup, which had raised roughly $30M from investors, was founded by ex-Apple (AAPL) employees. It's unclear what OpenAI will do with the team and technology from Glass Imaging, but the Sam Altman-led company is working on a series of smart devices that are set to be released in the coming months. One such device could be a smart speaker in the shape of a puck that will cost more than $300.
  • OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

data.title: Trump doubles down on $5K dividend as midterm odds favor Democrats
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday pushed back on Democratic criticism regarding his proposed $5K "Trump dividend," insisting the payout will happen if voters elect a Republican Congress in the upcoming midterm elections.

In a Truth Social post, Trump claimed the dividend is made possible because the country is generating "Trillions of Dollars of Economic Development, Investment, and Pure SUCCESS". He dismissed opposition from Democrats—whom he referred to as “Dumocrats”—saying they hope the policy never happens.

Defending his ability to deliver, Trump pointed to past legislative achievements and last year's $1,776 financial gift to the military as proof of his follow-through, stating, "When I say something, I mean it!". 

Meanwhile. the president's $5K-per-person pledge faces three major hurdles: finding the money for a payout that could cost more than $1T, getting Congress to approve the spending, and overcoming legal questions over whether tying the payment to a Republican victory amounts to an election bribe.

Despite Trump's assurances that a dividend "will happen," prediction markets suggest the necessary Republican sweep faces steep odds. Kalshi traders are assigning only a 16% chance that Republicans will retain both the House and the Senate.

Conversely, a Democratic sweep of both chambers is the favored outcome at 49%, while a split Congress featuring a Democratic House and Republican Senate sits at 36%.

The midterms are 49 days away from Nov. 3rd.

data.title: August rally cools, but the ETF industry still posts a fresh AUM high
data.description:
U.S. ETF assets under management rose to $16.39T at the end of August from $15.79T on July 31, LSEG Lipper data shows. Net inflows of $176.3B combined with market performance to produce the $609B increase.

Equity ETFs led the month with $94B in new money, followed by bond ETFs at $55.8B. Alternatives gathered $12.3B, commodities $11B, money-market products $2.1B, and mixed-asset funds $0.9B. 

The inflows arrived while global equities advanced, although the rally grew less assured as August progressed. Demand remained broad-based across asset classes even as investor conviction moderated later in the period. The result was another month of expansion for the U.S. ETF industry, with both flows and price appreciation lifting assets to a fresh high.

data.title: GE Vernova sinks 9% as GLJ Research starts with Sell rating, Street-low $470 PT
data.description:
GE Vernova (GEV) plunged 8.6% in Monday's trading as GLJ Research slammed the stock with a Sell rating and a Street-low $470 price target, calling the company "a cyclical gas turbine manufacturer priced as a secular compounder," while the shares trade near $880.

The company is the day's worst performer in the power infrastructure sector that is moving broadly lower, extending a slide that had already been underway; GE Vernova (GEV) shares are still up by a third YTD even after Monday's move, but they are down 16% over the past month.

GE Vernova (GEV) "is a cyclical industrial, and it is priced as a software company," according to GLJ's Gordon Johnson, noting at 38.9x forward EV/EBITDA, the stock trades at nearly 4x the multiple of Micron, a business whose earnings are also a function of an industry supply/demand balance it does not control. 

"Gas turbines have had two full boom-bust cycles in the lifetime of most of the people who cover the stock. The market has decided this time is different. We think it has decided too early," Johnson wrote.

GE Vernova's (GEV) order-to-delivery lag has stretched to 4-5 years, which pushes the best pricing into 2029 and the cycle risk into 2030, the analyst said, asserting that everything ordered in 2026 and 2027 delivers into 2030-31, when his supply model has effective industry capacity at 104-113 GW against orders of 88-90 GW.
